facts.statement: The genus is known from a single tooth that was first figured by Ernst Stromer in 1933 and named by Oskar Kuhn in 1936.
facts.quote: The genus is known from a single tooth, which was first figured by Ernst Stromer in 1933, and then named as a new genus of the family Goniopholididae by Oskar Kuhn in 1936.

facts.statement: In 1979, Éric Buffetaut and P. Taquet reclassified the tooth as belonging to the family Trematochampsidae.
facts.quote: In 1979, Éric Buffetaut and P. Taquet instead referred the tooth to Trematochampsidae.

facts.statement: Fossils of Baharijodon come from the Bahariya Formation in Egypt, dating to the Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: It is known from the Bahariya Formation in Egypt, which dates back to the Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Baharijodon lived between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago during the Cenomanian.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Baharijodon belongs to the parent group Crocodylia.
Baharijodon is classified within the class Reptilia.

rejected.statement: Baharijodon is an extinct genus of trematochampsid crocodylomorph.
rejected.quote: Baharijodon is an extinct genus of trematochampsid crocodylomorph.
